plan.summary: Provision a containerized GKE Autopilot stream processor cluster with Workload Identity Federation consuming from Cloud Pub/Sub and aggregating metrics into Firestore.
plan.architecture_overview: A private GKE Autopilot cluster deployed in us-central1 running inside a custom VPC with dedicated secondary CIDRs for pods and services. Workload Identity Federation binds the Kubernetes Service Account (sa-stream-worker in stream-apps namespace) to a dedicated GCP IAM Service Account with least-privilege roles (roles/pubsub.subscriber and roles/datastore.user). The Python asyncio stream processing application pulls events in batches of up to 50 messages from Pub/Sub subscription 'stream-gke-sub', calculates 1-minute tumbling window metrics (throughput, latency, error rate), and persists aggregations to Firestore. Manifests define a Deployment with resource requests (cpu: 250m, memory: 512Mi), health probes, and a HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaling up to 2 replicas at 80% CPU.

plan.risk_assessment: GKE Autopilot provisioning involves heavy stateful operations typically taking 10-15 minutes. Subnet secondary CIDR ranges must be allocated accurately prior to cluster creation to prevent deployment failures. Image build must precede manifest application to avoid ImagePullBackOff pod crashes.
